exercises.name: Pelvic floor lift and release with exhales
Sit-to-stand to a chair or bench
Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor coordination
Glute bridge with 2-second hold at top
Plank from knees or incline plank
Goblet squat to a low box or chair
Step-up (max controlled reps each side with dumbbell)

notes: Stay well short of fatigue in week 1.
Each exercise is 2 sets of 6 to 8 slow reps, or the time listed. Rest 30 to 60 seconds between exercises.
Session structure: Warm-up (5 min), main work (25 min), cool-down and breathing (5 min).
No jumping, hopping, skipping, running, or high-impact cardio until cleared.
She should be able to hold a conversation throughout.
Exhale on effort, inhale on return. No breath-holding or straining. Coordinate a gentle pelvic floor lift on the exhale.
Three sessions per week, roughly 35 to 40 minutes, with at least one rest day between them.
Daily walks: add these outside sessions from Week 1, building duration each week.
Conditioning (at end of session): 8 to 10 minutes of brisk walking, stationary bike, or low-intensity step-touches at RPE 6.

Baseline tests (end of session, one attempt each): wall sit hold, glute bridge max reps at 2-second hold, plank max hold time, step-up max controlled reps each side with dumbbell, two-minute brisk walk (distance or HR recovery), pelvic floor check.
Record all baseline numbers and her RPE ratings across the block.
Confirm OB's clearance for jumping and higher-impact work at the 14-week mark. Do not start impact work until that is confirmed.
If pelvic floor symptoms, diastasis concerns, or persistent pain, refer to a women's health or pelvic floor physiotherapist before loading further.
Next phase can introduce tempo and unilateral strength, progressing to light plyometric preparation (pogo hops, then low-amplitude jumps) only after clearance and symptom-free progress.

# 4-Week Postpartum On-Ramp Block (Weeks 10 to 13 Postpartum)

**Goal:** Rebuild movement quality, pelvic floor and deep core coordination, and general work capacity without impact. At the end of this block she should be able to perform a full set of bodyweight and light-dumbbell movements with good control, so you can progress to jumping at the 14-week mark once her OB confirms.

## Before Week 1: Intake Checks

Clarify these before the first session, since they change the programme:

- **Delivery type:** C-section recovery may need more time on abdominal and loaded trunk work.
- **Diastasis recti:** Check for doming or coning during a crunch-style movement, or have her self-check at the midline. Mild separation is common. Doming or coning means regress the trunk work.
- **Pelvic floor symptoms:** Any leaking with coughing, sneezing, or exercise; heaviness or pressure in the pelvis; pain with intercourse. Any of these means a pelvic floor physio referral before progressing loaded work.
- **Breastfeeding:** Affects hydration and fuelling. Schedule sessions around feeds where possible.
- **Sleep and stress:** Low sleep will blunt recovery. Adjust volume rather than pushing through.
- **Her own goals and any pain:** Note any musculoskeletal pain (back, hips, wrists) from carrying and feeding.

**Red flags that stop the session and trigger a referral back to her GP/OB:** heavy bleeding, chest pain, dizziness, calf pain or swelling, pelvic pain that worsens, or a bulge at the vaginal opening.

## Programme Principles

- **Effort:** Week 1 is RPE 4 to 5 out of 10. Week 2 is RPE 5 to 6. Week 3 is RPE 6. Week 4 is RPE 6 to 7. She should be able to hold a conversation throughout.
- **Breathing:** Exhale on effort, inhale on return. No breath-holding or straining. Coordinate a gentle pelvic floor lift on the exhale.
- **Impact:** None. No jumping, hopping, skipping, running, or high-impact cardio until cleared.
- **Frequency:** Three sessions per week, roughly 35 to 40 minutes, with at least one rest day between them.
- **Session structure:** Warm-up (5 min), main work (25 min), cool-down and breathing (5 min).
- **Daily walks:** Add these outside sessions from Week 1, building duration each week.

---

## Week 1: Acclimatisation (Weeks 10 to 11)

**Purpose:** Reconnect with breathing, pelvic floor, and basic movement patterns. No dumbbells this week. Stay well short of fatigue. If she feels good afterwards, that is the right dose.

**Session structure:** Each exercise is 2 sets of 6 to 8 slow reps, or the time listed. Rest 30 to 60 seconds between exercises.

**Warm-up:**
- Diaphragmatic breathing in supine, 2 minutes.
- Pelvic floor "lift and release" with exhales, 8 reps.
- Cat-cow, slow, 6 reps.

**Main work:**
- **Heel slides** (supine): slowly slide one heel out and back, keeping the lower back neutral, 6 each side.
- **Glute bridge** (bodyweight): drive through heels, exhale on the way up, 8 reps.
- **Dead bug, heel taps only** (supine): arms up, one leg tapping down to the floor, 6 each side. Stop if the midline bulges.
- **Wall or incline push-up:** hands on a counter or wall, controlled, 8 reps.
- **Bird dog:** on hands and knees, slow extension of opposite arm and leg, 6 each side.
- **Sit-to-stand to a chair or bench:** controlled descent, 8 reps. Use the hands to assist if needed.
- **Standing march:** 2 minutes, with breath control.

**Cool-down:** Diaphragmatic breathing, 2 minutes. Gentle hip flexor and chest stretch, 30 seconds each.

**Daily walks:** 10 to 15 minutes at an easy pace.

---

## Week 2: First Loading (Weeks 11 to 12)

**Purpose:** Introduce light dumbbells and slightly more volume. Begin building single-leg control.

**Equipment:** Dumbbells at 2 to 4 kg (start at 2 kg for most lifts).

**Warm-up:**
- Diaphragmatic breathing with pelvic floor coordination, 2 minutes.
- Glute bridge march, 8 each side.
- Standing arm circles and hip circles, 1 minute.

**Main work (2 to 3 sets each):**
- **Goblet squat to box:** 8 to 10 reps, 2 kg dumbbell held at chest. Box at a height she can control.
- **Glute bridge with 2-second hold at top:** 10 reps, optional dumbbell across hips.
- **Standing dumbbell row:** hinge at the hips with a flat back, row to the ribs, 8 to 10 reps each arm.
- **Half-kneeling or staggered-stance dumbbell press:** 8 to 10 reps each arm, 2 kg.
- **Dead bug, full version:** alternate arm and leg, 8 each side. Regress to heel taps if doming appears.
- **Side plank on knees:** 15 to 20 seconds each side.
- **Low step-up** (step height she can control, no push-off jump): 8 each side, holding a light dumbbell or using hands on a rail.

**Cool-down:** Diaphragmatic breathing and a hamstring and hip flexor stretch, 2 minutes total.

**Daily walks:** 15 to 20 minutes.

---

## Week 3: Building Capacity (Weeks 12 to 13)

**Purpose:** Increase load and volume, add single-leg strength, and introduce low-impact conditioning.

**Equipment:** Dumbbells at 4 to 6 kg.

**Warm-up:**
- Breathing and pelvic floor coordination, 2 minutes.
- Bodyweight squat to box, 8 reps.
- Glute bridge, 10 reps.

**Main work (3 sets each):**
- **Goblet squat to box:** 8 to 10 reps, 4 to 6 kg. Slow 3-second lowering phase.
- **Romanian deadlift with light dumbbells:** 8 to 10 reps, flat back, hinge focus, 4 to 6 kg.
- **Split squat (static lunge):** 6 to 8 reps each side, bodyweight or light dumbbell, with a stable hand on a wall if needed.
- **Single-arm dumbbell row:** 8 to 10 reps each arm, 4 to 6 kg, bracing on a bench or table.
- **Incline dumbbell press:** 8 to 10 reps, bench or counter at an incline, 4 to 6 kg.
- **Dead bug, full version:** 8 to 10 reps each side, slow tempo.
- **Plank from knees or incline plank:** 20 to 30 seconds, stopping if doming or pelvic discomfort appears.
- **Farmer carry:** walk 20 to 30 metres holding two dumbbells at 4 to 6 kg, steady posture and breathing.

**Conditioning (at end of session):** 8 to 10 minutes of brisk walking, stationary bike, or low-intensity step-touches at RPE 6.

**Daily walks:** 20 to 30 minutes.

---

## Week 4: Consolidation and Baseline Testing (Weeks 13 to 14)

**Purpose:** Consolidate the block and establish baseline numbers you can build on in the next phase.

**Equipment:** Dumbbells at 4 to 8 kg, depending on how Week 3 felt. Only increase if the RPE stayed at 6 or below.

**Warm-up:**
- Breathing and pelvic floor, 2 minutes.
- Glute bridge, 10 reps.
- Dead bug, 6 each side.

**Main work (3 sets each, or as noted):**
- **Goblet squat to a low box or chair:** 10 reps, 6 to 8 kg.
- **Romanian deadlift:** 10 reps, 6 to 8 kg.
- **Split squat:** 8 reps each side, 4 to 6 kg.
- **Single-arm dumbbell row:** 10 reps each arm, 6 to 8 kg.
- **Incline dumbbell press:** 10 reps, 6 to 8 kg.
- **Side plank, knees or full:** 20 to 30 seconds each side.
- **Step-up, moderate height:** 10 each side, light dumbbell.
- **Farmer carry:** 30 to 40 metres, 6 to 8 kg in each hand.

**Baseline tests (end of session, one attempt each):**
- Wall sit hold: maximum time, to 30 seconds or stopping at form breakdown.
- Glute bridge: maximum reps at a 2-second hold, in one set.
- Plank (knees or incline): maximum hold time.
- Step-up: maximum controlled reps each side with a 2 to 4 kg dumbbell.
- Two-minute brisk walk: distance covered, or heart rate recovery after one minute.
- Pelvic floor check: confirm no leaking or heaviness during the session.

**Cool-down:** Full-body breathing and stretching, 5 minutes.

**Daily walks:** 25 to 30 minutes.

---

## Handover at End of Week 4

- Record all baseline numbers and her RPE ratings across the block.
- Confirm her OB's clearance for jumping and higher-impact work at the 14-week mark. Do not start impact work until that is confirmed.
- If she has any pelvic floor symptoms, diastasis concerns, or persistent pain, refer to a women's health or pelvic floor physiotherapist before loading further.
- Next phase can introduce tempo and unilateral strength, progressing to light plyometric preparation (pogo hops, then low-amplitude jumps) only after clearance and symptom-free progress.
